notes.text: Data rate up to 800 kbit/s.
Dual signal wires: a failed LED does not break the chain (backup input BIN).
Bit timing: T0H 220–380 ns, T1H/T0L/T1L 580 ns–1 µs; reset (frame) low time above 280 µs.
Data order GRB, high bit first.
No external parts needed, not even a capacitor.
Reverse-connection protection: a reversed 5 V supply does not damage the LED.
VIH is 0.7·VDD: 3.5 V at VDD 5 V, above a 3.3 V GPIO high level.
Common practice for a 5 V strip on a 3.3 V ESP32: a 5 V-supplied buffer with TTL inputs (e.g. 74AHCT125) in the data line.
Typical application (image only, p. 4): DO and BO of one LED feed DIN and BIN of the next; the first LED's BIN is often tied to GND or to DIN on strips (wiring not in the text layer).

interfaces.note: single-wire NZR, 800 kbit/s, 24 bit per LED in GRB order, two data inputs (pp. 1-4)

current.note: LED current: 12 mA per colour is the test condition of the brightness table (p. 3); the absolute maximum table gives a power consumption of 0.1–0.18 W per LED (p. 2).

hazards.text: 12 V LED supply (strips draw several amperes): keep the 12 V rail away from the ESP32 and from the data inputs (max 5.7 V); power the ESP32 from its own regulator and share only GND.

notes.text: 12 V supply reduces the current of the whole pixel and the voltage drop along the strip.
Data rate 800 kbit/s.
Two-way signal transmission: a damaged pixel does not affect the rest of the chain.
notes.evidence: Realize two-way signal transmission, in the case of damage to a

notes.text: Bit timing: T0H 220–380 ns, T1H 580–840 ns, T0L 900 ns–5 µs, T1L 600 ns–5 µs; reset low time above 280 µs.
Data order GRB, high bit first.
Power consumption 0.1–0.18 W per LED (absolute maximum table).
VIH is a fixed 2.7 V at VDD 12 V (not relative to the 12 V supply).
The data inputs tolerate at most 5.7 V (absolute maximum): never pull them up to the 12 V supply.
On WS2815 strips the second data input (DIN2/BIN) of the first LED is usually tied to GND or DIN1 (strip vendor practice, not in the datasheet text).
